brief: Design an interface for a "conversation archaeologist" tool where users excavate buried text messages from old chat logs by literally brushing away layers of digital sediment with their cursor, reveal

dominant_strengths: The brown sediment-like background tone vaguely gestures toward the archaeology metaphor in the brief
Subtle grid pattern hints at a workspace canvas, providing minimal texture against flat fill
dominant_weaknesses: Effectively empty canvas: no typography, no UI chrome, no excavation tool, no chat artifacts, no interaction affordances visible
Brief demands a tactile brushing-away interaction with revealed text layers — none of that mechanic, content, or feedback exists
Zero information hierarchy, no system, no branding, no state — the design simply does not exist as a product
fix_priorities: Build the core excavation surface: layered sediment textures, a brush cursor, and progressively revealed message fragments
Introduce typography for unearthed messages with timestamp/depth metadata to convey archaeological framing
Add toolbar, layer depth indicator, and discovered-fragments archive to make the metaphor functional
Establish a palette beyond flat brown — dust, parchment, ink — to give material credibility
rationale.norman_balance: All three Norman layers fail simultaneously: nothing to feel viscerally, nothing to operate behaviorally, nothing to reflect on conceptually.
rationale.intent_fit: The screenshot shows an essentially blank brown canvas with a header bar and does not implement any aspect of the conversation-excavation brief.
